criteria.description: Personally implement program logic for a stated task in an explicitly named programming language; a language listing alone is insufficient.
Describe at least one relevant implementation mechanism, such as functions, control flow, data handling, or an applied library operation, in that programming work.
Perform a basic check of that program behavior, such as a test case, expected-output comparison, or diagnosis of an execution problem; a numeric improvement is not required.
Demonstrate explicit study or explanation of algorithms or data structures, or personal implementation/analysis of a specified mechanism; a degree or component name alone is insufficient.
Identify relevant processing steps, data-structure operations, an invariant, or computational complexity; using a library without such detail is insufficient.
Explain or check correctness, a boundary case, or a time/space property for that mechanism; a worked course example can qualify.
Personally design or implement an explicitly described object-oriented structure or design pattern; using an OO-capable language alone is insufficient.
Describe class responsibilities, object collaboration, encapsulation, interfaces, or polymorphism in that design.
Check or explain how the design supports a concrete behavior, substitutability, separation of concerns, or a change scenario; organization-wide architecture is not required.
Personally use an identified AI assistant to write, inspect, test, or improve software for a stated development task.
Describe how the assistant output was incorporated, revised, constrained, or reviewed in the development workflow.
Check generated or suggested code against intended software behavior, tests, or source-code inspection; trusting the assistant output alone is insufficient.
Personally design software components or interfaces for a stated problem, with explicit component boundaries or interactions; implementation alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant interface, data/control flow, or design choice linking those components; a small project design can qualify.
Check the design against a concrete requirement, interaction scenario, or constraint; production scale and architecture ownership are not prerequisites.
Personally implement server-side behavior, a route, or an API contract for a stated function; consuming another service alone is insufficient.
Describe relevant request/response handling, data access, validation, or error handling in that backend implementation.
Exercise or test the backend behavior using a request, integration check, or expected response, including a stated success or failure case.
Personally implement a user interface or client-side behavior for a stated application; an isolated analytical chart alone is insufficient.
Describe relevant interaction, state, component, rendering, layout, or accessibility behavior in that implementation.
Check a user interaction, rendering behavior, accessibility condition, or expected client response; formal user studies are not required.
Personally design, implement, or diagnose communication, coordination, shared state, or isolation across explicitly separate services/processes/nodes or tenants.
Describe the cross-boundary mechanism, such as messages, replication, partitioning, consistency, or tenant isolation; a tool name alone is insufficient.
Check or reason through a concrete cross-boundary scenario such as failure, ordering, duplicate delivery, consistency, or isolation; a small prototype can qualify.
Personally query, design, migrate, or access explicitly relational data using SQL or a stated relational mechanism; generic JSON is insufficient.
Describe a relevant query, join, aggregation, key, constraint, schema relationship, or migration operation.
Check the relational operation or returned data against expected records, counts, constraints, or a stated query purpose.
Personally use a named non-relational store or search system for a stated data/search task; generic database work alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant document/key/index/query/search mechanism used in that task.
Check retrieved results, storage behavior, query correctness, or a relevant edge case for that system.
Personally apply an explicit maintainability practice such as refactoring, modularization, clearer contracts, or reducing code complexity.
Describe the concrete code organization, interface, duplication, naming, or complexity issue addressed and how it was addressed.
Check preserved behavior, clearer usage, or maintainability of the changed code through tests, inspection, or a concrete change scenario.
Personally design, implement, or execute software tests for stated software behavior; unrelated model evaluation is insufficient.
Describe a test input/setup, expected behavior, assertion, or coverage case relevant to that software.
Inspect test outcomes or use tests to verify expected behavior or a fix; comparative performance gains are not required.
Personally reproduce, trace, isolate, diagnose, or correct a stated software fault; merely seeing a failed status is insufficient.
Describe a diagnostic step, hypothesis, log/trace inspection, or isolation method related to that fault.
Check the diagnosis or fix by rerunning the failing case, inspecting the relevant state, or comparing actual and expected behavior.
Personally review source code or a proposed implementation, or participate explicitly in source-code/PR review; merging or document review alone is insufficient.
Identify a concrete implementation concern or review focus, such as correctness, maintainability, security, or test coverage.
Provide or respond to actionable code feedback, or check the resulting revision; approval alone without the reviewed concern is insufficient.
Personally use an explicit version-control system through commits, branches, diffs, merges, or pull requests; a repository link alone is insufficient.
Describe a concrete source-control workflow or operation such as branching, comparing changes, resolving a conflict, or managing a revision.
Check or reconcile the resulting change history, diff, merged state, or restored revision; a complex enterprise workflow is not required.
Personally use an identified cloud provider/service for a stated computing, storage, deployment, or operational task.
Describe relevant service configuration, permissions, resource setup, or integration for that task; do not infer other providers.
Check service access, execution, deployment behavior, resource state, or an expected cloud result.
Personally build, configure, or run a container or explicitly containerized workload; ordinary deployment alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant image, dependency, port, volume, environment, or orchestration configuration; Docker does not imply Kubernetes.
Check container startup, application execution, connectivity, isolation, or reproducibility for that workload.
Personally automate a build, test, release, infrastructure-provisioning, or configuration step; ordinary Git use is insufficient.
Describe a relevant workflow trigger, sequence, artifact, environment, or configuration in that automation.
Check the automated step through its output, run status with diagnostic inspection, resulting artifact, or a test deployment.
Personally measure, analyze, or optimize a stated software/system performance property such as latency, throughput, or resource usage.
Describe the measured workload, profiling method, bottleneck, or optimization mechanism; an unexplained percentage is insufficient.
Check the relevant performance behavior using a stated measurement or observation; positive improvement and production scale are not required.
Personally implement or use logs, metrics, traces, alerts, monitoring, or maintenance for a running software system; ordinary progress reports are insufficient.
Describe the operational signal, instrumentation, alert condition, or diagnostic/maintenance workflow used.
Use that signal or workflow to check system behavior, investigate an operational issue, or verify the monitoring/maintenance action.
Personally handle a stated software failure, recovery, load, redundancy, or scaling concern; simply calling a system robust is insufficient.
Describe the relevant mechanism, such as retries, recovery, limits, redundancy, or controlled scaling.
Check a failure, recovery, load, or correctness scenario related to that mechanism; large production traffic is not required.
Personally implement or test an explicit software-security control such as authentication, authorization, secure access, or a vulnerability mitigation.
Describe the protected resource, trust boundary, permission rule, threat, or secure mechanism involved.
Check an allowed/denied access case or relevant security behavior; content moderation and ordinary input checks alone are insufficient.
Personally use SQL or explicit relational querying to answer an analytical question or access relevant data.
Describe a relevant selection, filter, join, aggregation, or relational relationship used for that analytical task.
Check query outputs against expected counts, known records, join behavior, or the analytical question.
Personally write code or scripts for a stated data-transformation or analysis task in an identified language or analytical library.
Describe a relevant transformation, calculation, data structure, or analytical procedure implemented.
Check the script output, data transformation, or analytical result against an expected property or independent calculation.
Personally perform a stated analytical task in a spreadsheet using formulas, pivots, or another analytical operation; a static table alone is insufficient.
Describe the formula, aggregation, lookup, pivot configuration, or spreadsheet workflow used.
Check spreadsheet results, input ranges, formula behavior, or reconciliation with source data.
Personally inspect, compare, or interpret data to answer a stated question; collecting or displaying data alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant analytical comparison, grouping, calculation, or inspection method.
Interpret a finding or check the analysis against data quality, alternative explanations, or the original question; business impact is not required.
Personally define or analyze a business/product metric or decision-relevant business question; a business title alone is insufficient.
Describe the metric definition, comparison, segment, or analytical procedure connecting data to that question.
Interpret or check the business meaning and a limitation of the result, or connect it to a concrete decision; realized revenue impact is not required.
Personally elicit, clarify, analyze, or translate a stakeholder/problem requirement; receiving instructions alone is insufficient.
Describe a concrete ambiguity, acceptance condition, data need, metric definition, or requirement translation addressed.
Check the interpreted requirement with stakeholder feedback, a documented acceptance condition, or a worked scenario.
Demonstrate explicit study or explanation of statistical concepts/methods, or personal application of a statistical method; a degree or percentage alone is insufficient.
Identify the relevant statistical method, quantity, assumption, or interpretation; a generic software name alone is insufficient.
Interpret a statistical result or assess an assumption, uncertainty, or limitation in a worked example or actual analysis.
Personally design or run an experiment with explicit comparison groups, treatments, or conditions; ordinary implementation iterations are insufficient.
Describe the comparison setup, assignment/control, outcome measure, or confounding consideration.
Evaluate or interpret the comparison, including an observed result, uncertainty, or design limitation; a positive treatment effect is not required.
Demonstrate explicit study, explanation, or application of a causal-inference method aimed at estimating a causal effect; correlation or prediction alone is insufficient.
Identify a causal identification strategy, comparison, intervention, confounder adjustment, or explicit identifying assumption.
Explain or check an identification assumption, bias risk, validity limit, or interpretation of a causal estimate in a worked example or actual analysis.
Personally build or operate a repeatable ingestion, transformation, or ETL flow with stated source and destination stages; a one-off download is insufficient.
Describe a relevant extraction, transformation, dependency, scheduling, or loading mechanism.
Check a run, data transfer, schema, row count, or failure condition in that repeatable flow.
Personally design an explicit data schema, entities/relationships, dimensions, or analytical data structure; outputting JSON alone is insufficient.
Describe relevant keys, relationships, grain, dimensions, constraints, or representation choices in that model.
Check the model against a query/use case, data consistency condition, relationship, or analytical requirement.
Personally clean, validate, reconcile, prepare, or govern a stated dataset; storing data alone is insufficient.
Describe the quality issue and a relevant rule or transformation, such as missing-value handling, deduplication, validation, or reconciliation.
Check the resulting data or quality rule against expected values, counts, consistency, or documented exceptions.
Personally build or maintain an analytical/business dashboard with stated metrics or analytical views; an isolated chart or document is insufficient.
Describe a dashboard metric, data connection, filter, interaction, layout decision, or refresh behavior.
Check a displayed metric, filter, refresh, or dashboard interaction against its data source or intended use.
Personally create or design a data visualization to communicate a stated analytical quantity or relationship.
Describe the chart type, visual encoding, grouping, axis, or design choice appropriate to the data/question.
Check the displayed data or interpretability through value validation, scale/label inspection, or audience feedback.
Personally use an explicitly identified BI platform for a stated analytical activity; a generic chart alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant BI data connection, model, measure, visual, filter, or report operation in that platform.
Check the resulting BI output or behavior against source data, an expected calculation, or a stated analytical requirement.
Demonstrate explicit study, explanation, or personal use of data-warehouse concepts or an identified warehouse in an analytical context; an ordinary database alone is insufficient.
Identify a warehouse-specific analytical structure or operation, such as fact/dimension modeling, analytical loading, partitioning, or warehouse querying.
Explain or check a warehouse query, load, grain, reconciliation, or analytical use case; a worked learning example can qualify.
Demonstrate explicit knowledge of large/distributed data processing or personal work with an explicitly described scale/distribution constraint; a framework name alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant partitioning, distributed transformation, memory/resource, shuffle, or scale-handling mechanism.
Explain or check correctness or resource behavior for the stated workload/mechanism; a bounded distributed learning example can qualify.
Personally automate or orchestrate a repeatable analytical/data workflow; a one-off manually executed analysis is insufficient.
Describe the repeated steps, trigger, dependency, scheduling, or orchestration logic.
Check an automated run, produced artifact, dependency, or failure-handling behavior against the intended workflow.
Personally implement program logic for a stated task in an explicitly named non-Python language; Python-only work is outside this core.
Describe a relevant function, control flow, data structure, or applied library operation in that non-Python implementation.
Check the program behavior with a test, expected-output comparison, or diagnosis of an execution problem.
Personally implement Python logic or use an explicitly supported Python library for a stated task; do not infer Python from a finished AI tool or a teammate contribution.
Describe a relevant Python operation, data manipulation, function, library procedure, or integration in that implementation.
Check the Python program or data output against an expected behavior, test case, or diagnostic observation; numeric improvement is not required.
Personally implement, test, debug, maintain, or build an API in a concrete software context; using a finished AI product alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant engineering mechanism such as module/interface organization, input/error handling, a test, or a diagnostic procedure.
Check software behavior or an engineering change against an expected requirement, test, or failure scenario.
Personally query, design, or access explicitly relational data through SQL or a stated relational operation; generic JSON is insufficient.
Describe a relevant query, join, aggregation, key, schema relationship, or relational access operation.
Check the operation or returned data against expected records, counts, constraints, or the stated data task.
Personally apply an explicitly identified ML method/framework in a stated modeling task; calling a finished AI product alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant modeling procedure involving inputs, model choice, fitting, prediction, or an ML-specific configuration.
Check model behavior using relevant data, criteria, a metric, or error inspection; production deployment and improved benchmark scores are not required.
Personally work with an explicitly identified neural/deep-learning architecture in a stated training or inference task.
Describe a relevant neural-model input, architecture component, training/inference configuration, or tensor/model operation.
Check neural-model behavior, outputs, training behavior, or errors using a relevant basic evaluation; training from scratch is not required.
Demonstrate explicit study, explanation, or application of mathematical, probability, or statistical foundations; a degree or numerical output alone is insufficient.
Identify a relevant mathematical/statistical concept, equation, method, or assumption rather than only an umbrella field name.
Interpret, derive, apply, or check that concept in a worked example or actual task, including a relevant property or limitation.
Personally clean, label, validate, structure, or prepare data for a stated ML/analytical task; saving model output alone is insufficient.
Describe the relevant preparation rule or transformation and the data issue or representation it addresses.
Check prepared data against expected labels, schema, ranges, consistency, leakage concerns, or another relevant quality property.
Personally build or operate a repeatable ingestion, transformation, or processing flow for data; one-off loading or an inference call alone is insufficient.
Describe the source/destination stages and a relevant transformation, dependency, scheduling, or loading mechanism.
Check data movement, a pipeline run, data quality, or a failure case for that flow.
Personally create, select, or transform input features actually used by a model; formatting outputs or product features is insufficient.
Describe a feature construction, encoding, selection, transformation, or representation and its relationship to model inputs.
Check the engineered features through value inspection, leakage/consistency checks, or a relevant model comparison.
Personally fit or update model parameters through an explicitly described training process; inference, API integration, and prompt editing are insufficient.
Describe a relevant training dataset, objective, optimization step, hyperparameter, or training configuration.
Check training behavior or the trained model through loss monitoring, validation data, output inspection, or another relevant evaluation; gains are not required.
Personally adapt a pretrained model by updating its weights or trainable adaptation parameters; prompt editing and training from scratch alone are insufficient.
Describe the adaptation data, trainable components, procedure, or configuration, such as an explicitly applied parameter-efficient technique.
Check the adapted model or adaptation process using relevant validation data, outputs, training behavior, or a comparison; improved results are not required.
Personally evaluate model quality or behavior against stated data, criteria, metrics, or error categories; successful execution alone is insufficient.
Describe the evaluation dataset/setup, metric, rubric, error-analysis procedure, or comparison appropriate to the model task.
Inspect or interpret an evaluation finding or a limitation of the evaluation; a quantitative improvement is not required.
Personally design or run an explicit controlled/comparative model experiment, ablation, or test; ordinary iterative implementation is insufficient.
Describe the compared conditions, changed factor, controlled setup, or outcome measure.
Inspect or interpret the comparison or its limitations; a favorable or statistically significant result is not required.
Personally implement, configure, launch, or operate a runnable model-inference serving path or endpoint; a notebook or request to someone else model API alone is insufficient.
Describe how a request/input reaches the model and produces a served response, or a relevant serving/runtime configuration; local serving can qualify.
Check the serving path with an inference request, response validation, startup/runtime check, or a relevant error case; cloud/production scale is not required.
Personally apply an ML lifecycle operation such as model/data versioning, a reproducible ML workflow, model monitoring, or continuous model delivery.
Describe the relevant artifact tracking, reproducibility, monitoring, pipeline, or delivery mechanism; an isolated training run or generic CI is insufficient.
Check model artifact identity, reproducibility, lifecycle execution, monitoring behavior, or delivery state for that ML operation.
Personally configure or operate cloud, compute, container, distributed, or operational infrastructure for an explicit AI workload; a cloud AI API call alone is insufficient.
Describe a relevant compute/resource, environment, dependency, container, execution, or infrastructure configuration for that workload.
Check AI workload execution, resource behavior, environment setup, or infrastructure operation; large clusters and production traffic are not required.
Personally use or build an explicitly generative system for a stated content-generation task; unspecified AI or classification alone is insufficient.
Describe the actual input/output modality and a relevant generation configuration, integration, or workflow.
Inspect or check generated content against a stated task criterion, constraint, or quality issue; model training is not required.
Personally use or develop with an explicitly identified language model for a stated language task; unspecified AI work is insufficient.
Describe the model input, output, prompting configuration, context handling, or application integration relevant to that task.
Check language-model behavior or output against a stated requirement, example, or error category; this does not establish training, RAG, or agents.
Personally implement or use a described retrieval-to-generation workflow in which external retrieved context grounds generated answers; embeddings or search alone are insufficient.
Describe how relevant external context is retrieved and passed into generation; identify an actual linkage rather than two unrelated tool names.
Check retrieved context relevance, grounded-answer correctness, citations, or a retrieval/generation failure case in that workflow.
Personally design or implement a model-mediated tool/action workflow with explicit invocation, result handling, or control flow; an agent project name alone is insufficient.
Describe a concrete tool/action input, returned result, control decision, or bounded/human-reviewed execution step in that workflow.
Check tool/action execution or result handling against intended behavior, an error case, or a control constraint; autonomy and multiple tools are not required.
Personally design, refine, or evaluate prompts for a defined model behavior; a casual question or merely saying a prompt was followed is insufficient.
Describe an explicit prompt technique or design element, such as instructions, examples, output constraints, context organization, or a targeted revision.
Check the resulting behavior against examples, constraints, errors, or a defined evaluation criterion; numeric improvement is not required.
Personally use embeddings, similarity search, vector indexing, or vector storage for a stated retrieval/representation task; generic arrays or LLM use are insufficient.
Describe the embedding, similarity, indexing, query, or vector-storage mechanism applied to that task.
Check retrieved matches, representation behavior, indexing/query correctness, or relevance against examples or a stated criterion; a full RAG pipeline is not required.
